## What This Is

Claude Code supports a persistent, file-based memory system that loads context across sessions. Until now, the Sovereign Ecosystem template documented the boundary principle — vault files are canonical, chat memory is not — but gave no guidance on how to configure that memory system when you do choose to use it.

This update adds an `# auto memory` section to the CLAUDE.md template. It documents the modular architecture pattern: a thin index file pointing to individual typed memory files, rather than a single monolithic document that grows unwieldy over time.

## What It Adds / Changes

- New `# auto memory` section in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- Documents the modular index pattern: `MEMORY.md` as a thin index only (under 200 lines), individual files per memory entry
- Defines four memory types: `user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference`
- Specifies frontmatter format for individual memory files (name, description, type, last_updated)
- Explicitly lists what NOT to save (code patterns, file paths, git history, anything already in vault files)
- States the boundary rule: vault state takes precedence over memory when they conflict

## How to Implement

1. Create the memory directory: `~/.claude/projects/[encoded-cwd]/memory/`
   - The encoded path matches your vault root. Claude Code will use this automatically.
   - On macOS/Linux: `~/.claude/projects/[encoded]/memory/`
   - On Windows: `C:\Users\[You]\.claude\projects\[encoded]\memory\`

2. Create `MEMORY.md` inside that directory as a thin index. Example:

   ```markdown
   # Sovereign Ecosystem — Claude Code Memory

   ## User
   - [user_role.md](user_role.md) — Sovereign's role and domain focus

   ## Feedback
   - [feedback_tone.md](feedback_tone.md) — preferred tone and response style

   ## System
   - [system_structure.md](system_structure.md) — vault structure and key file paths
   ```

3. Create individual memory files with this frontmatter:

   ```
   ---
   name: Sovereign Role
   description: Who the Sovereign is and what they are building — used to frame responses
   type: user
   last_updated: YYYY-MM-DD
   ---

   [memory content here]
   ```

4. Let Claude Code populate memory organically over time. You can also ask it explicitly: "Save this to memory" for preferences or decisions worth preserving across sessions.

5. CLAUDE.md already handles the rest. The boundary rule is in place: vault files are authoritative, memory is context.

## Prerequisites

Session 1 (Vault Initialization and Adapter Setup) should be complete. Claude Code must be your active AI interface.

## Optional?

No — this is a core CLAUDE.md update. But setting up the memory directory is optional. The section documents the pattern; you do not need to act on it immediately.
